data.one_liner: A lightweight Dart client for communicating with a Redis server.
data.what_it_does: Provides a Dart API to connect to a Redis server, execute commands like set, get, delete, and close the connection. Supports TLS, authentication, and several Redis data types including strings, JSON, and time series.
use_when: You need fast, in‑memory caching or pub/sub via Redis from a Flutter/Dart app
Your backend already uses Redis and you want a direct client without an HTTP layer
avoid_when: You require offline‑first storage on the device
You need a relational or NoSQL database on the device
strengths: TLS and credential support for secure connections
Supports multiple Redis data types (strings, JSON, TimeSeries)
Pure Dart, no native plugins required
weaknesses: Only works with a reachable Redis server; no offline fallback
Limited to Redis functionality; not a full‑featured database
